market.headline: Indexes ended almost flat, but Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit dominated the day: money moved out of NVDA and into AMD, and a hot inflation report keeps rate-hike risk alive into tomorrow's PPI.
market.day_type: News-driven rotation inside chips. Index damage stayed small (SPY -0.4%, QQQ -0.3%, volume light at 0.7x normal), while NVDA traded 4.4x its usual volume on the CEO news and buyers rotated into AMD.
watch: PPI Fri 08:30: a second hot inflation print after October's CPI keeps Fed hike talk alive and pressures expensive tech
QQQ 679.84 (today's low) and 694.56 (today's high); SPY 753.70 and 763.03. A break of the lows means the rebound is over
AMAT, CSCO and NBIS results tonight (dates estimated); NVDA reports Nov 17 (estimated) and sets the tone for every chip stock here

stocks.headline: Morning call: right. CEO Jensen Huang is out. The stock fell 4.3% to 166.19 on 4.4x normal volume, touched a 52-week low of 148.80, then closed near the day's high.
stocks.why: This is a people problem and not yet a business problem. Sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and next year's profit forecasts rose 24% in 90 days. The stock now trades at 10.3x next year's profit, its cheapest in 5 years. The rebound from 148.80 to a close near 167.14, on very heavy volume, looks like forced sellers being cleared out. The real risk is the probe: reports tie Huang's personal links to a Huawei-linked investor, and an outside law firm is investigating. If that turns into export-control or China trouble, it hits sales, not just sentiment. The fallout also reaches AMD (gaining share of investor money), TSM, MU, SMCI and AVGO (suppliers), and CRWV and ORCL, where the market is now questioning AI financing.

long_term.reason: The business is accelerating and the price is the cheapest in 5 years. Brokers cut targets (Goldman to 220, BMO to 240, Citi to 225) but kept Buy ratings, so they are not abandoning the stock.

stocks.what_would_change_it: News that the probe found leaked technology or lost customers, or a weak outlook with no named CEO on Nov 17, would turn this into Avoid.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open. Buy a small starter only if it holds above 158.78 after the first hour, and save the rest of the position for after the Nov 17 report.

levels.means: above = the panic low holds; below = sellers are back in control, so stay out
above = today's reversal is confirmed; below = still stuck in the selloff range
above = it has recovered the whole CEO-news drop; below = the damage is not repaired yet

stocks.headline: Morning call: right. Up 5.9% to 585.30 on 1.7x normal volume, a new 20-day high of 594.00, and up 44.7% in 5 days.
stocks.why: AMD is where chip buyers went when they left Nvidia. The business supports the move: sales are up 45% and speeding up, it has beaten forecasts 5 quarters in a row, and next year's profit forecast rose 15% in 90 days. William Blair and Oppenheimer upgraded it. But a 44.7% run in a week means a lot of good news is already priced in at 31x next year's profit. If Nvidia names a strong CEO or delivers a big report on Nov 17, money flows back and AMD gives up part of this run.

long_term.reason: Accelerating sales and rising forecasts justify owning it, but not at any price after a one-week sprint.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A clean Nvidia CEO handover or a strong NVDA report would end the rotation and make AMD a Hold.
stocks.action: Don't chase above 594.00 tomorrow. Buy only on a pullback that holds 567.65 after the first hour.
